target_customer: US Air Force and commercial customers for adversary air training drones, with quiet supersonic airliners as the long term goal
problem: Fighter pilots lacked affordable supersonic adversary aircraft for training, and no quiet supersonic passenger aircraft existed.
business_model: Government contracts (SBIR and AFWERX) funding drone development, plus venture capital

founders.name: Norris Tie
founders.background_notes: YC page says about three years as a propulsion engineer on supersonic vehicles; employer not named.

founders.name: Tim MacDonald
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder of the supersonic aircraft startup; no details.

exit.reason: Company said it could not find the traction needed to continue and could not cover cash needs without further customer support; core design tool suite offered as IP

competitors.name: Aerion
competitors.what: Developing the AS2 supersonic business jet

competitors.name: Spike Aerospace
competitors.what: Developing the S-512 quiet supersonic business jet

technical_complexity.rationale: Supersonic flight vehicles and low boom airliner design require hardware, certification and engine breakthroughs far beyond a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Government relationships and aircraft design know-how were hard to copy, but no patents or contracts large enough to lock in were cited.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals pursued airliners and business jets; no one bought Exosonic, and it wound down in November 2024.

market_need_then: NASA signed a 247.5M dollar contract with Lockheed for the X-59 in 2019 and several startups raised for supersonic travel; Air Force adversary air training demand led to SBIR awards from 2021.

identity.logo: Standard logo lockup file seen in search results; no design description

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Flying Magazine, New Atlas, Business Insider and TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Wide trade press and national outlets for a small startup, though no source discusses the brand itself.

pivots.to: Supersonic adversary air UAV for the Air Force as stepping stone
pivots.why: Government SBIR funding and a nearer term market; first AFWERX award in 2021

outcome_analysis: Exosonic raised a seed above 4 million dollars in 2022 plus AFWERX contracts and flew a subscale Trident test vehicle in April 2024. It announced shutdown on November 8, 2024, saying it could not find the traction to continue and lacked customer support to cover cash needs. A hard-tech airliner and drone program needed far more capital than the seed and grants supplied.
notes: The 2021 grant amount (750K reported) and the 2023 grant come from search result summaries, not opened pages. YC page says 4.5M+ private capital and 2M+ AFWERX; other pages say 3M+ AFWERX (unverified conflict). Total raised exceeds the recorded seed, so earlier private money (from 2019 to 2021) is unfound. A salestools.io page claims 38M Series A at 150M valuation and CB Insights lists 250K over 8 rounds; both rejected as unverifiable. Shutdown date came from the opened airframer release; the exosonic.com page returned 503. The pivot is inferred from the YC description and AFWERX contract timing; treat as approximate. Competitor sources opened only as search results.
